# Accessibility

SeniorMode's READMEs use the same section order so readers can find installation, examples, and the Skill Directory in any language. We aim to keep the documentation usable with a keyboard, a screen reader, and a narrow viewport.

## How we write and review the documentation

- Use headings in a logical order. Give sections names that help readers find them in a screen reader's heading list.
- Write link labels that describe the destination or action. Give badges, charts, and other meaningful images text alternatives. Keep instructions and essential information available as text.
- Check that links and expandable sections can be reached and activated with the keyboard. Make sure their labels and reading order make sense with a screen reader.
- Give language links their native names and language tags. Review the language menu and examples in right-to-left languages. Keep shell commands and configuration examples in left-to-right order.
- Check the layout at narrow viewport widths and with browser zoom. Use compact tables and keep long commands in code blocks. Review images and text in GitHub's light and dark themes.

## Report an accessibility barrier

Use the [accessibility and bug report form](https://github.com/EnesKeremAYDIN/SeniorMode/issues/new?template=bug.yml). Include the page link and language, what you were trying to do, what happened, and what you expected. If relevant, add the browser, operating system, assistive technology, and exact keystrokes or screen reader announcement. Share only what you are comfortable posting publicly.
